<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Circle</title>
  <style>
    * {
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
      box-sizing: border-box;
    }
    body {
      width: 100vw;
      height: 100vh;
      display: flex;
      justify-content: center;
      align-items: center;
      background: #f5f5f7;
    }
    svg {
      width: min(400px, 80vw);
      height: min(400px, 80vw);
      filter: drop-shadow(0 4px 12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.15));
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <svg id="ae683f770" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
    <title id="circle-title">A solid circle</title>
    <defs>
      <radialGradient id="circleGradient" cx="35%" cy="35%" r="75%">
        <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#6ea8fe"/>
        <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#2563eb"/>
      </radialGradient>
    </defs>
    <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="196" fill="url(#circleGradient)"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
Changes made:
- Added an accessible `<title>`/`role="img"` for screen readers, and a more descriptive page `<title>`.
- Replaced the flat black fill with a subtle radial gradient + drop shadow for visual depth.
- Made the SVG responsively sized (`min(400px, 80vw)`) so it scales on small screens instead of overflowing.
- Reduced the radius slightly (196 vs 200) so the shadow/stroke doesn't get clipped by the viewBox, and gave the page a light background for contrast.
